personality: 1 iOS-Native Clean structure with 4 Tactile / Playful pill elements and rounded cards
personality_one_liner: A modern, trust-focused community mobility platform that feels youthful, safe, and distinctly unlike traditional ride-hailing apps.

spacing.rule: Generous vertical breathing room for content, strict single column for form inputs, minimum 56pt height for tappable rows. Padding must be intentional and soft to match the friendly feel.

do's: Use glassmorphism for the bottom tab bar
Use frosted glass overlays on featured Mission1000 banners or sticky headers during scroll
Apply translucent tinted base underneath foreground content to guarantee readability
dont's: Never apply glass to dense route lists, body content, or form fields
Do not blur basic list rows or chips

screens.name: Splash & Onboarding
screens.purpose: Introduce the Mission1000 eco-friendly traffic initiative and brand identity.
screens.layout: Full-bleed imagery with a top-to-bottom vertical linear gradient scrim (transparent to 80% surfaceInverse). Primary CTA (pill) pinned to the bottom 1/3 inside safe area.

screens.name: Auth Flow (Login / OTP)
screens.purpose: Verify user identity securely with high trust markers.
screens.layout: Clean, distraction-free single column. Large typography for instructions. Forms use floating-free labels. KeyboardAvoidingView with CTA pinned above the keyboard.

screens.name: Home & Ride Search
screens.purpose: Switch between Instant, Daily, and Planned modes and initiate a ride twin search.

states.empty: Friendly illustration explaining how to find a ride twin

screens.layout: Top sticky segmented control (pill style) for Instant/Daily/Planned. Followed by a Mission1000 featured banner card. The bottom area contains vertically stacked, tap-based ActionCards for available routes. Each route card anchors the duration/time top-left and price right. Keep cards minimal (max 6 data points) on white surfaceSecondary with soft shadows to ensure scannability.

screens.name: Create Ride
screens.purpose: Allow drivers to post their route, vehicle, and price details easily.
screens.layout: Multi-step or long-scroll form. Single column layout. Use steppers for seats, a slider for price, and highly visible pill chips for selecting ride type. Sticky 'Publish Ride' button at the bottom.

screens.name: Messages & Profile
screens.purpose: Manage connections, verifications, wallet rewards, and chats.

states.empty: Empty state illustration with 'No active chats/rides'

screens.layout: Standard list view with minimum 56pt tappable rows. Profile utilizes a top hero banner section (tinted brand background) with overlapping avatar. Wallet shows a prominent Balance card with a 3D icon and transaction history stacked vertically below.

onboarding_mission1000.alt: Clean green urban city road representing Mission1000 traffic reduction

ride_twin_match.alt: Smiling woman driving, representing a friendly ride twin

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly follow the user's color palette: LinQ Blue (#2453C8) is the hero color. Dark navy (#172033) is for primary text. Use the provided soft border (#E8ECF3). NO other blues or purples are permitted.
The layout must prioritize a premium iOS-Native Clean structure but inject tactile warmth using pill-shaped (999) buttons, pill segmented controls, and rounded cards (md/lg).
Font weight cap is 500. Use Plus Jakarta Sans for all typography. Create visual hierarchy through size and color/opacity, not by using weights like 600/700/Bold.

For the Ride matching/Discovery cards, implement the 'ActionCard' pattern. Keep each card to a maximum of 6 data points, pinning the most critical information (Time/Duration) to the top-left, and price on the right. Avoid excessive infographics on the cards.
Implement a top-to-bottom gradient scrim (transparent to 70-80% surfaceInverse) on the onboarding/splash image to ensure any overlaid white text is WCAG AA readable.
Buttons should always be sticky at the bottom for major actions (like 'Request Unlock' or 'Publish Ride') above the safe area, avoiding the need for users to scroll to act.
Ensure all interactive elements have a minimum 44x44pt touch target. Use hitSlop if the visual component is smaller.
